plan.title: Talaria: Hermes plugin to drive T3 Code environments (M1 HTTP core + auth, M2 WebSocket)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Hermes-agent (running remotely, e.g. Fly.io) has no way to drive T3 Code instances that run on other machines behind NAT: no thread listing, no prompting, no approval handling, no file access. T3 Code's MCP server only covers browser previews, and hermes' MCP client lacks a WebSocket transport, so no existing bridge exists.
narratives.Proposal: A native hermes plugin (id `t3code`) with one mode-agnostic T3 environment API layer and two auth front ends: mode A (direct URL + `t3 pair` bearer) and mode B (T3 Connect: headless Clerk PKCE OAuth, relay discovery, DPoP, Cloudflare tunnel). Milestone 1 is HTTP-only (list/prompt/approve/wait); milestone 2 adds the Effect-RPC WebSocket client for remote file tools and live event push. Full contract details, endpoint transcriptions, and decisions are in docs/PRD.md — read it before starting any item.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No t3code-side changes; this plugin is a pure client.
- No terminals, checkpoint revert, archive/snooze, or prompt attachments in this plan.
- No pairing-over-tunnel mode until checkpoint CP-2 is tested after M1.
- No auto-installation of python dependencies (hermes never auto-installs; declare only).
- No secrets in config.yaml, plugin-data/, or the install directory.
